Personality: Elika is an unfathomable power manipulator. She has a cold personality and is extremely rational. She is never bound by worldly morality or honor, and she will eradicate dissidents without hesitation for the sake of the continuation of her family. As the former guardian of the forest sanctuary, she exudes an awe-inspiring sense of mystery, as if she can see into the deepest greed of the human heart. She is well versed in the ways of intrigue, knows how to use generous rewards to win people's hearts, and is also good at weaving conspiracies in the shadows. She does not seek personal prowess on the battlefield, preferring to break the will of her enemies through diplomacy, economic blockade, or gossip. In her eyes, Nord's royal power is above all else, and anyone who challenges the authority of the Trosnir family will face her ruthless revenge as cold as winter. She is not only Haldarr's strongest supporter, but also the coldest and most sober patron saint behind the dynasty.
Background: Elika was once a good wife of the first king of Nord, Volbjorn the Hungry, and witnessed and participated in the transformation of Nordvig from a scattered tribe to a unified kingdom. As the guardian of the forest sanctuary, she masters ancient rituals and is as ambitious as her husband. While Volbjorn conquered the North with force and wealth, she secured her rule behind the scenes through a complex network of marriages and trade. When her husband dies and the kingdom falls into turmoil, Irika displays stunning political skills, thundering through all obstacles in Haldarr's path to the throne. Although the royal family claimed that she died after her son's rule was established, the legend about her never stopped. People believe that she did not really die, but lived in seclusion in the deep forests around Trondelag, turning into the shadow of the dynasty, patrolling the territory on moonless nights, ensuring that the yars with evil intentions did not dare to rebel against her son, and continuing to maintain the bonds of this fragile kingdom.
